text:
jen: Hey team — escalating from a customer (integration) who sees the Streaming API return invalid JSON after a reconnect/resume. They say the stream looks fine at first then after a network hiccup the resumed data leaves the client with an incomplete JSON object (parse error).

lina: Do we have any server-side logs showing a truncated chunk or missing `finish_reason` on resume?

jen: Here's the repro they provided (redacted):
```
Client: connect SSE /v1/streams?model=redwood-x
SSE chunk 1: event: data
data: {"id":"abc","choices":[{"text":"Hello\n","index":0}]}

(disconnect)
(reconnect using Last-Event-ID: abc)
SSE chunk 2: event: data
data: {"id":"abc","choices":[{"text":"world","index":0}]}

But client reports final payload on resume is: `\{"id\":\"abc\",\"choices\":\[\{\"text\":\"Hello\nworld\"` and then parse error — missing closing `}]}`.
```

jen: They also attached this snippet from their client logs: `Unexpected end of JSON input at position 178` after reconnect.

tom: Hmm. Could be that when we resend the trailing chunk we skip sending the final event terminator, or the last-chunk had a flush that got lost. Any reverse-proxy (nginx/ALB) in front that might buffer/zip?

alex: We had a similar symptom in the past where the resume flow wrote the second half of the JSON in a separate SSE `data:` event but missed a final empty `data:` sentinel that the client expects. Check codepath: `resume_stream()` -> `write_partial()` -> `flush_final()` — there's a race with connection close.

jen: Customer environment: Node client using `eventsource` polyfill, reconnect enabled, using Last-Event-ID. They said they only see the truncated JSON when reconnect frequency is high (~2-5s).

lina: Can we reproduce quickly with a test harness? I can run a local loop that forcibly closes the socket and then reconnects with Last-Event-ID.

jen: They included HTTP debug headers from the resume request: `Connection: keep-alive`, `Last-Event-ID: abc`, `Accept: text/event-stream` and server responded 200 OK streaming. No explicit `Content-Length`.

alex: If Content-Length is missing (chunked transfer), and we have an abrupt TCP close, some clients may not get the final CRLFCRLF boundary — causing the last JSON to be received incomplete. Workaround could be to emit a final small sentinel event like `data: {"__stream_end":true}` before closing. But that's a protocol change.

tom: Action items for triage: 1) eng-runtime reproduce locally 2) capture raw bytes at edge when resume occurs 3) check history for regressions in resume/flush paths (PRs in last 30d) 4) give customer a mitigation they can deploy.

lina: I'm on 1). Starting a harness now: script will open SSE, send chunk, force-close, reconnect with Last-Event-ID, verify final byte sequence.

jen: Customer says current mitigation they tried: client retries and then concatenates two last events manually — fragile. They want us to guarantee well-formed JSON after resume.

lina: Update from repro: I can reproduce an edge-case where the final `data:` line is emitted but the TCP connection closes before the trailing `\n\n` sequence is flushed. Raw capture shows bytes end with `..."world"` with no closing `}]}`. That matches customer.

alex: Root cause likely: flush_final() triggers but returns before kernel actually transmits last few bytes due to nonblocking write + connection close. Need to ensure we do a blocking flush or wait for write completion or use `SO_LINGER` semantics for resume path.

tom: Also check our proxy timeout/keepalive. If proxy detects an idle stream and tears it down mid-flush, same symptom. Which proxies are in path for hosted customers? ALB + envoy. Envoy had a known issue with streaming flush backpressure in older versions.

jen: Customer is on hosted API (not private). Could be our edge envoy cluster.

lina: Quick mitigation we can push on runtime: when handling a resume (Last-Event-ID), delay sending connection close for 200ms after final write to ensure kernel buffers drain. Small latency tradeoff but increases correctness. I can draft a patch.

alex: Agreed, do defensive write completion or short delay. Also add unit/integration test that simulates abrupt close and verifies final JSON integrity.

jen: Customer asked about `finish_reason` specifically — they say sometimes the resumed payload lacks `finish_reason` field and client code expects that to decide end-of-stream. That aligns: missing trailing bytes mean the `finish_reason` key and closing structure can be lost.

tom: OK, assign: @lina to prototype flush/wait patch; @alex to look at envoy versions and ALB config; @jen to give customer temporary guidance: increase client reconnect backoff and implement a small post-reconnect validation (if parse error, retry fetch last N tokens via non-stream endpoint).

jen: I'll message the customer with repro steps and a suggested client-side workaround. Ticket #INC-2026-874.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: runtime/resume-flush-wait (canary) -> ETA 2h (simulated) :gear:

lina: Patch posted to PR 4523, includes test harness and 200ms linger option behind feature flag `stream_resume_strict_flush`.

alex: If deploy passes canary, we should gradually enable feature globally and monitor `stream.resume.parse_errors` metric.

jen: Thanks all. I'll follow up with the customer once the canary is live. :thumbsup:

tom: Logging note: add tracing tag `resume_id` and log bytes-sent/bytes-acked for resumes so we can correlate with customer partials in future.

jen: Closing loop: I'll update this thread with canary results and customer response.
